text:
elaine_sales: Heads-up: QuantHealth kickoff this morning. They're requesting an EU-only data path for model inference and audit logs + BYOK. Need to confirm routing policy, subprocessor list limited to EU, and impact on monitoring. Can folks triage?
tariq_se: Quick clarifying Qs: 1) Is the ask strict 'no outbound to non-EU' for any telemetry? 2) Is control-plane traffic allowed through our global control plane if masked?
anya_privacy: Customer statement: "All data and logs must remain in EU. Control-plane may be global only if no identifying telemetry leaves EU and keys remain under customer control (BYOK)." They will want subprocessors inventory and a short signed attestation.
felix_infra: For Dedicated and Private we can pin tenant traffic to eu-west-1 GPUs and set failover to eu-central-1 only. We currently forward aggregated metrics to vendor-metrics-us by default; we can flip to vendor-metrics-eu for this tenant with a toggle. Toggle requires ticket and change window.
elaine_sales: They're also worried about latency: target is <=120ms p95 for inference. Workload: mostly short calls but with occasional 500-token sequences. They want capacity guidance and a cost estimate for reserved vs burst.
tariq_se: Architecture note: continuous batching improves throughput but can add tail latency; we should recommend smaller batch caps for p95 target. Also recommend quantized model variant for cost.
anya_privacy: BYOK options: we support KMS keys in eu-west-1 and also customer-provided keys via a KMIP/HSM integration (enterprise). We will not escrow or store plaintext keys. Drafting attestation template now — will include subprocessor list and telemetry routing commitments.
felix_infra: Logged infra task: ENABLE-EU-METRICS-998 (ops-bot created ticket). ETA for metrics route change: 3 business days if low-risk. Live change needs a config flag and an infra rollout.
ops-bot: Ticket ENABLE-EU-METRICS-998 created and assigned to felix_infra.
elaine_sales: Can someone paste a sample routing header/policy we can include in the SOW? Needs to be readable for legal.
tariq_se: Sample JSON routing directive we can embed:
```
X-Redwood-Residency: {"preferred_region":"eu-west-1","allowed_failovers":["eu-central-1"],"telemetry_endpoint":"eu","control_plane_mode":"masked"}
```
Note: control_plane_mode=masked means only non-identifying metrics are sent if allowed.
anya_privacy: Masking: we replace tenant_id/tenant_ip with hash and drop payload traces. Full traces are disabled unless customer enables. This reduces debugging detail and may affect time-to-resolution for incidents. Call out in SOW.
felix_infra: SLA: Serving SLA for Dedicated doesn't change. Observability SLA (debug traces, live sampling) will be reduced while masking is active. We'll outline which features are restricted.
elaine_sales: Pricing ask: give a ballpark for reserved capacity to support 300 rps, p95 120ms, median seq ~256 tokens. Also per-GB egress estimate for eu-west-1.
felix_infra: Back-of-envelope: concurrency ~36 (300*rps*0.12s). For target model we expect ~1-2 GPUs per 100 rps (model dependent). Reserved monthly seat for 2-4 GPUs + buffer. Egress: ~0.08 USD/GB in eu-west-1 (estimate). Finance will provide exact numbers.
anya_privacy: I'll attach subprocessor inventory filtered to EU-only and a redacted global list for legal. Customer will likely ask for a signed addendum for no non-EU processors.
elaine_sales: Ok next actions: 1) Fel ix to open infra change and capacity model (include exact GPU counts). 2) Anya to send attestation + subprocessors. 3) Tariq to craft SOW snippet with routing directive and feature impacts. I'll bundle into a one-pager for QuantHealth.
ops-bot: Reminder: schedule a short tech handoff call with QuantHealth once docs are ready.
elaine_sales: Thanks all — aiming to have draft brief + numbers in 4 business days. :slightly_smiling_face:
